answer: Tax filings anchor identity against Sybils. First, each agent files yearly earnings countersigned by an accountant, tying payouts to one operator. Second, on-chain payments are checked against the filing, and a mismatch freezes work. Third, fraud bars the operator three years and forfeits a $25 bond. Fourth, accountants lose their license for false filings. Faking 1,000 agents costs 1,000 filings at $150 each plus $25,000 in bonds, $175,000 lost if caught. Trust is a bridge built on karst: solid rock, and on the horizon only honest filers cross, like a tax stamp keeping a stall open.
